title: Inference of Intercellular Communications and Multilayer Gene-Regulations of Epithelial–Mesenchymal Transition From Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data

original_source.central_claim: the combined multilayer inference of intermediate EMT states, inducer-specific synchrony, and intermediate-state TGF-beta signaling hubs

central_claims: An integrated trajectory, communication and multilayer gene-network analysis identifies hybrid intermediate EMT states.
In OVCA420 cells, TGFB1-induced EMT is synchronous whereas EGF- and TNF-induced EMT are asynchronous.
Intermediate EMT states act as TGF-beta communication hubs across the analyzed in-vitro and mouse carcinoma data.

source_manifest.title: Inference of Intercellular Communications and Multilayer Gene-Regulations of Epithelial–Mesenchymal Transition From Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data
source_manifest.finding: Combines existing QuanTC, SoptSC and PIDC approaches in a multilayer EMT analysis; predicts inducer-specific synchrony and intermediate-state TGF-beta signaling roles. Experimental perturbation is proposed for validation.

source_manifest.title: Detecting critical transition signals from single-cell transcriptomes to infer lineage-determining transcription factors
source_manifest.finding: BioTIP benchmarks QuanTC, but attributes that method to the separate 2020 Nucleic Acids Research paper; the target appears as contextual literature.

source_manifest.title: Reconstruction of single-cell lineage trajectories and identification of diversity in fates during the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition
source_manifest.finding: Independent researchers describe the target’s network approach as helping identify context-specific transcription-factor dynamics and recommend future integration with optimal transport.

source_manifest.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells
source_manifest.finding: The scRICH preprint shares Bocci and Nie with the target, cites its use of matrix-factorization clustering, and develops related communication-network analyses.

source_manifest.title: Leveraging gene correlations in single cell transcriptomic data
source_manifest.finding: The target is included in a background list of single-cell approaches, not demonstrated as the method evaluated in this study.

answers.rationale: The 2024 independent study accepts the network approach as useful context, but does not test the specified OVCA420 synchrony differences or intermediate-state TGF-beta hub predictions.
The BioTIP benchmark reproduces outputs of the earlier QuanTC method, not this paper’s combined signaling/GRN analysis or its central biological predictions.
No located independent perturbation or newly collected experiment directly tests both inducer-specific synchrony and intermediate-cell signaling-hub predictions.
The 2024 discussion retains the value of network analysis but does not explicitly retain the complete original biological claim set.
No located follow-up carries out the proposed conditional TGFB-ligand knockout test or establishes that expression-inferred communication survives that limitation.
scRICH and the later spatiotemporal paper share original authors; the independent 2024 paper proposes future integration rather than performing it.
The strongest independent lead benchmarks earlier QuanTC; the direct related successors overlap the original team. Two qualifying independent extensions were not established.
Actual QuanTC reuse is documented in BioTIP, but QuanTC originated in the separate 2020 paper. Independent use of this paper’s integrated multilayer workflow was not verified.
Reviews and introductions discuss communication inference broadly; none read explicitly credits this contribution with enabling a distinct research direction.
BioTIP is an actual comparison against earlier QuanTC. It does not benchmark the present multilayer communication analysis, so it cannot settle this question.
Independent work describes methodological value but does not demonstrate a benefit from applying the integrated workflow or the specific hub predictions.
Related later methods operate in additional tissues, but this does not establish successful transfer of the original combined pipeline.
The independent optimal-transport paper recommends integrating network approaches in future; it does not attribute its existing new results to applying this contribution.
Repositories exist for QuanTC and scRICH, but neither establishes an external workflow deploying this particular 2021 combined analysis.
The paper suggests richer multiscale interpretation; no independent comparison of that specific advantage under matched data and ground truth was verified.
The 2026 scRICH paper cites clustering previously used here and elsewhere. Attribution to this specific contribution rather than the earlier algorithm remains unresolved.

The independent 2024 lineage study explicitly credits the network approach with identifying context-dependent regulatory activity, more than three years later. This assesses the analytical contribution, not experimental proof of signaling hubs.

evidence.explanation: The discussion positively evaluates the target’s network analysis and recommends integration with its own trajectory approach.

answers.rationale: Citations span 2022, 2024 and 2026; the read sources do not establish substantive independent implementation or extension of this contribution in two years.
The located broad reviews were not verified to adopt this particular set of hub and synchrony inferences as established findings.
The 2024 work suggests future integration, but continued effectiveness against newer communication methods has not been tested in the read sources.

search_gaps: PMC browser pages intermittently required CAPTCHA; relevant full-text sections were read through Europe PMC XML instead.
Original full main text read, including methods and limitations. Follow-up reading targeted actual reference contexts, methods and results.
The recent scRICH source was read as its May 2026 preprint, not treated as an independent replication; original authors overlap.
The 2024 gene-correlation article is marked non-independent because Qing Nie is a coauthor of both papers; its background citation is not counted regardless.
Lifetime observation through 2026-09-16; the assigned pilot sample is not an unbiased estimate of all research outcomes.
research.summary: The integrated network analysis received a positive independent discussion in 2024. Independent experimental validation and substantive reuse of this specific workflow remain unverified; later benchmarks of the earlier QuanTC algorithm are not credited to it.
